fix(psram): give the system heap the unused tail of PSRAM\_SECTION

ai\_agent could not be started at all on this configuration. The Wi-Fi stack that arrived with the last upstream sync took static RAM from 97KB to 182KB, which left the SRAM heap with a 158KB arena, 27KB free and a 26312-byte largest block -- smaller than the agent task's 32768-byte stack. NSH reports a failed spawn as "command not found", so this looked like a missing builtin even though 'help' listed it. Meanwhile 16MB of PSRAM was already mapped, powered and probed, and none of it was reachable from malloc(): this file's pools and AP heap are only visible through bk7258\_psram\_alloc(), and the 6MB PSRAM\_SECTION linker region had nothing in it at all. bk7258\_psram\_initialize() now hands the unused tail of PSRAM\_SECTION to the system heap. The tail is measured from \_\_ap\_psram\_noinit\_end, so placing data in .psram.data/.psram.bss/.psram.noinit keeps working and just shrinks what the heap receives. It has to happen here rather than in arm\_addregion(): that runs while nx\_start() is setting up the heap, and PSRAM has no power until the CP answers the power-up request over the mailbox. Measured, ai\_agent config: before 157976 arena 27120 free 26312 largest agent will not start after 6449416 arena 6318528 free agent ready in 929ms vela> heap\_info Heap: arena=6449416 fordblks(free)=6110144 uordblks(used)=339272 vela> net\_status Network connected: yes The trade is that PSRAM is non-cacheable and mm cannot steer allocations, so some buffers that used to be in SRAM now are not: camera\_preview's expression render went from 37ms to 67ms per frame. For a configuration that otherwise cannot run the agent at all, that is the right side of the trade; steering specific allocations back to SRAM is a separate job.
